name: org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin
description: The MCP Server Maven Plugin integrates a Machai Model Context Protocol (MCP) server into a Maven build. It provides aggregator goals named stateless and streamable that configure and start stateless HTTP or streamable HTTP MCP servers using the Maven project's name, version, and base directory. The plugin loads a PropertiesConfigurator from a configurable properties file, applies configured parameters to JVM system properties without overriding existing values, registers configured Machai tools, and exposes them to MCP clients. It is designed for local development, integration testing, demonstrations, and build automation, including multi-module reactor use where an aggregator goal starts one server for the build. It includes a lifecycle function tool that can initiate delayed shutdown of the hosting JVM.

constructors.description: Creates the Maven Mojo for the stateless HTTP MCP server goal. Maven normally instantiates this Mojo when the stateless goal is invoked; users configure and run it through Maven rather than constructing it directly.

Creates the Maven Mojo for the streamable HTTP MCP server goal. Maven normally instantiates this Mojo when the streamable goal is invoked; users configure and run it through Maven rather than constructing it directly.

features.name: stateless
features.description: Aggregator Maven goal that applies configured parameters, loads MCP server configuration, creates an HttpStatelessMcpServer from the Maven project name and version, supplies the project directory and port, and starts the stateless HTTP MCP server. Configuration or startup failures are reported as Maven execution errors.

examples.description: From a Maven project with a readable mcp.properties file, run the aggregator's stateless HTTP MCP endpoint on port 8080. Ensure the Maven plugin is available from the configured repository, replace the configuration path or port as needed, and connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the endpoint.

features.name: streamable
features.description: Aggregator Maven goal that applies configured parameters, loads MCP server configuration, creates an HttpStreamableMcpServer from the Maven project name and version, supplies the project directory and port, and starts the streamable HTTP MCP server. Configuration or startup failures are reported as Maven execution errors.

examples.description: Run the streamable HTTP MCP transport from the Maven project root. First make the plugin available from Maven Central or a configured repository, prepare the Machai MCP properties file, set the listening port and configuration path, and invoke this goal; then point a compatible MCP client at the resulting HTTP service.

features.name: applyParameters
features.description: Applies the configured params map as JVM system properties, only setting a property when it is not already set. This allows runtime or command-line system properties to take precedence over plugin-provided values. A failure while applying parameters is reported as MojoExecutionException.

features.name: loadConfigurator
features.description: Loads the PropertiesConfigurator for the supplied absolute configuration file path. The transport Mojos use this common operation to load MCP server and tool configuration before starting the server.

features.name: stop_mcp_server
features.description: Exposes a lifecycle function that logs the shutdown request, waits for a grace period, records final usage statistics, and exits the hosting JVM with the requested exit code. The default exit code is 0. This terminates the hosting Maven JVM, not merely the HTTP endpoint, so invoke it only when the server process should end.

customizations.name: params
customizations.description: Maven plugin configuration map for extra key/value parameters to be copied into JVM system properties. Existing system properties take precedence, and null values are ignored. Use this to supply server or tool settings when configuring a Maven invocation.

examples.description: Add the plugin configuration to the project's pom.xml to set the port and configuration file and to provide an additional system property. Keep credentials in a secure external mechanism rather than committing secrets. Invoke either the stateless or streamable goal after configuring it.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.mcp.maven.AbstractMCPServerMojo
studs.description: Shared base for the plugin's MCP server Mojos. It centralizes environment parameter application and loading of PropertiesConfigurator instances, allowing transport-specific goals to share configuration behavior.

examples.name: Install and run the stateless MCP server

steps.instruction: Use Java 17 or newer and Apache Maven, and ensure the configured repositories can resolve org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.3.
Create a Machai MCP server properties file named mcp.properties in the Maven project root. Add the server and tool configuration required by your deployment; keep credentials out of source control.

From the project root run mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.3:stateless -Dmcp.port=8080 -Dmcp.config=mcp.properties. Use the streamable goal instead when the MCP client expects streamable HTTP.
Connect an MCP-compatible HTTP client to the server endpoint on the selected port and use the tools provided by the loaded configuration.
When finished, the stop_mcp_server lifecycle tool can request shutdown; it exits the hosting JVM after its grace period, so use it only when ending the Maven server process is intended.

examples.name: Configure the plugin in a Maven project
examples.description: Add the plugin entry to the build/plugins section of pom.xml, adjust the port and configuration path, and add only non-sensitive system properties to params. Then invoke the plugin with mvn org.machanism.machai:mcp-server-maven-plugin:1.4.3:stateless or replace stateless with streamable. Maven's mcp.port and mcp.config properties can also be supplied on the command line; the configuration file defaults to mcp.properties and the port is required.
